name: LNX-DBMS
tagline: 1990s German client/server SQL database for Linux and Unix, bundled with and sold by S.u.S.E.
description: LNX-DBMS was a relational client/server database for Linux and Unix from Villwock Softwareentwicklung in Rieden, Germany, distributed through S.u.S.E.: version 3 shipped free on the S.u.S.E. Linux distribution and version 4 (around 1996) was sold for DM 240 per server. It offered ANSI SQL with transactions, locking, indexes, a clustered index layout on the file system, database procedures and rules, user management, online backup, and in V4 referential integrity and ALTER TABLE. Access came through ESQL/C, an ODBC driver aimed at Windows clients, a WWW interface, a Java API, a Python interface and a fast non-transactional bulk-load API (LNX-XA). It ran on Linux, SCO, OSF/1 on DEC Alpha and Siemens Nixdorf RM systems. It disappeared as PostgreSQL and MySQL took over Linux.
statusNote: Sold via S.u.S.E. in the mid/late 1990s; no longer available. PostgreSQL or MariaDB are the natural modern equivalents on Linux.

pricing.notes: V3 was included free with S.u.S.E. Linux; V4 server cost DM 240, with ODBC, WWW, Java, Python and XA add-ons at DM 50-150.

strengths: Shipped free (V3) with S.u.S.E. Linux, an early bundled SQL server for Linux users
Broad access options for its time: ESQL/C, ODBC, Java, Python and web
Online backup and referential integrity in a low-cost package
Bulk-load API about 100x faster than ESQL/C inserts
weaknesses: Discontinued; no documentation or binaries in circulation
useCases: History of commercial databases on early Linux
Context for S.u.S.E.'s 1990s commercial software catalogue
